Turning to group4 with values 4, 1, 2, I check their relative positions against the template — the distances match, so I test whether a 90-degree CCW rotation maps the template's offsets onto group4's offsets correctly.

Confirming the rotation checks out, I now apply that same CCW transform to every cell of the template object, mapping each (row, col) coordinate to its rotated position while keeping track of the associated value at each point.

The remaining points check out consistently. But when I test group 3 against the template using vectors between the marked cells, the offsets don't match the expected pattern from the key, which is strange since all partial occurrences should normally align. I need to recheck the row data around row 13 and 15 to see if I misread the color positions.

Then it clicks: these near-misses stay unchanged in the output, and importantly the template object itself gets erased from the grid entirely, not just used as a reference. So my rule should be: erase the template location, then only complete groups that genuinely match its shape.

Tracing group2's connectivity, I find it also has four distinct colors {5,2,4,1}, meaning it qualifies as a second template object alongside the first, so both get selected and covered by the erasing logic. Now I'm working through how the grid-building function maps these normalized patterns back onto their occurrences.

Checking group3 against group2's relative color layout, I find their transformations differ by a coordinate swap, suggesting group3 is a transposed (dmirror) version of group2's pattern.

I also test group4 against group2's key but the distances don't match, ruling it out. With no other matches found, I move to computing group2's normalized object so I can apply the dmirror transform at group3's location.

Transposing the object's cells and anchoring against group3's actual positions using the 2, 4, and 1 markers confirms the offset works consistently across all three points, so I can now determine the full set of painted cells.

Building the output grid, I'm erasing the original template rows and group2 cells to zero, then painting in the completed group3 and group4 cells at their proper offset positions row by row.
